recipes.name: Chicken and Broccoli Alfredo
ingredients_raw: 1 cup fresh or frozen broccoli flowerets
1 pound skinless, boneless chicken breast, cut into cubes
1 (10.75 ounce) can Campbell's® Condensed Cream of Mushroom Soup (Regular, 98% Fat Free or 25% Less Sodium)

steps.text: Cook linguine according to package directions. Add broccoli for last 4 minutes of cooking time. Drain.
Heat butter in skillet. Cook chicken until browned, stirring often.
Add soup, milk, cheese, black pepper and linguine mixture and heat through. Serve with additional Parmesan cheese.

raw_recipe.headline: Chicken and Broccoli Alfredo
raw_recipe.description: Linguini is mixed with pieces of tender chicken and broccoli flowerets and coated with a rich, satiny Alfredo sauce featuring Campbell’s® Condensed Cream of Mushroom Soup to make a quick and fabulous dish.

video.description: This dish is delicious, and so easy with Campbell's® Cream of Mushroom Soup.

review.reviewBody: This was a lot better tasting than I thought it would be (honestly, it was just as good as other, more time-intensive recipes for alfredo that I've made at home.) I used less chicken and used the breast of a rotisserie chicken just because that's what I had left over. This was pretty convenient, since using the already-cooked chicken cut the preparation time in half. I liked this dish with less chicken, and when I make it next time, I will add more broccoli, as I didn't think it had enough. The cook time for the broccoli was perfect - it was still nice and bright green with just a slight crunch to it. I personally thought this was fine with the cream of mushroom (I hate mushrooms, but I hardly noticed the tiny little pieces in there), but I think this dish could be done with just about any type of cream soup.

This is definitely a winner! Instead of cooking frozen veggies with the pasta, I sauteed fresh veg with the chicken in the pan. They were not overcooked and worked perfectly. I diced 2 lg chicken breasts, seasoned well, and put into hot olive oil and butter mixed. Right away I cut up 1/2 an onion, 2 cloves garlic, and added to the chicken. Then chopped whatever veggies I had on hand, tonight it was cauliflower and zucchini. And added to the partly cooked chicken, with more salt, pepper, herbs. The rest I did as written, except I used grated mozzarella and sprinkled the powdery type of parmesan at the end. Used whole wheat pasta and this was very flavorful and easy to make. Success!!

Excellent! We are vegetarians so I used Faux "chicken" from Trader Joe's, and I added sautéed fresh mushrooms, 3 cups fresh broccoli which I blanched, soy milk in place of cows milk, garlic powder. It had wonderful flavor but it was a little dry, (possibly because I added ingredients?). Pasta always soaks up the sauce in dishes, so, even though the flavor was great, I opened a jar of alfredo sauce and added just enough to moisten it more. This recipe still gets five stars in spite of my "doctoring" because to me there is nothing better than a good base recipe to play with.

This was delicious! I followed other reviews, added 2 Tbsp. Cream cheese, garlic, upped the broccoli to 2C, and since I love mushrooms (I know it’s not traditional Alfredo!) 2 Bella mushrooms sliced. I also added broccoli to end of cook time in cheese sauce instead of boiling. DELICIOUS!!! I’ll def make this again!

i cubed the 2 big thin breast still a little froze, i put them in a container & seasoned with spices & stir it, i used 2 cans of cream of mushroom soup half a cup of milk, half a cup of parmesan cheese & 1/4 cup pepper & used a whisk, i put it in my slow cooker, i started on low with lid up for awhile, then put on high, i used a bag of broccoli cuts & put them in when you want to, i like my broccoli a little crunchy, not mushy, yummy

Absolutely loved this dish! I did make a few minor changes as I was cooking. I used 1 1/2 cans of the Cream of Mushroom Soup and also I doubled the amount of butter that the recipe called for. Also, to save yourself time, buy a already made rotisserie chicken, chop up the pieces that you need, and reheat with the sauce in the skillet.

I used egg noodles since thatt's what I had. I try not to use canned soups so I made Quick Alfredo Sauce. The half cup of milk wasn't needed and since the Quick Alfredo Sauce used Parmesean cheese I didn't add any to the sauce but sprinkled some on at the table. Quick and easy meal.

I added 1/4 c. chopped sauted onion and 2 t. minced garlic and used rotini pasta in place of linguine. Everyone in my family had at least seconds - 2 people had thirds! Definitely will make this again. Thanks for sharing the recipe.

Very simple recipe. I added about a ¼ cup of sour cream, ¼ bar of cream cheese, 1 ½ tsp of garlic powder and/ increased the broccoli to 2 cups. I also added 1 ¼ cup of fresh grated Mozzarella and a little extra Parmesan right before serving. So Yummy! We loved it. Oh and the garlic bread is a must to top it off. I know I will be making this again... as well as continue experimenting with substitutions.

I had all ingredients handy for 1/2 recipe and it was Great! So with 1 rotisserie chicken I can make chicken noodle soup using 10 C. chix broth & the breast meat + this full recipe using thigh & leg meat + 2 wings to snack on!

Could not believe how delicious this was! I rarely cook with canned soup products, but this is one recipe I'll be making over and over and over again. I did jazz up the chicken a bit by marinating it in a little olive oil, red pepper flakes, garlic, salt & pepper for a good hour or so - but aside from that stayed true to recipe. Will double the amount of broccoli next time (personal preference) ... didn't weigh our chicken, but used 1 large and 1 medium size breast so it was probably pretty close to a pound. Served with romaine salad and garlic bread. Hubs has already had 2 plates and is claiming the last portion for his lunch tomorrow. Snap to make. Oh - forgot - I didn't use Parmesan cheese - used freshly grated Pecorino Romano which was perfect.
Good for a quick meal. Next time I will add garlic, some fresh mushrooms and maybe onion.

Really easy and tasty. Nothing super fancy, and it could certainly use some upgrades. But for a quick, easy, one-dish meal it's a keeper. We added some fresh mushrooms and sautéed them with the chicken when it was nearly ready. Also, didn't have cream of mushroom (What? I know!) so used cream of chicken, and that worked fine. Added some garlic powder and onion powder. There was not much of this left at the end of the meal.
I liked it quite a bit, as did my husband. I added mushrooms, onion, and garlic.
very good and simple. i used white pepper instead of black.i have made this many times and it always very good.
I hate it when people modify a recipe and then rate it. I am going to do just that 😁 I added onions, mushrooms and garlic and used cooked chicken thighs. It was very good and we have leftovers too.
My family and I have been using this recipe for years. Very very good. Doesn’t necessarily taste like alfredo but in and of itself is very delicious and it’s always eaten up!
